name: Electrolytic capacitors
summary: Aluminium electrolytic capacitors that store and smooth DC on nearly every power board.
uses: Repairing power supplies, TVs and routers (bad capacitors are the commonest fault)
Buffering a motor or LED driver
identify: Cylinders in a printed sleeve with a stripe marking the negative leg, and a value in µF and volts. Big snap-in ones (200–450V) sit by the mains input of power supplies and can hold a dangerous charge after unplugging; camera flashes hold a 330V one.
test: A domed or leaking top means it’s dead. Discharge big ones through a resistor, then check with a capacitance meter: the reading should be close to the label.

decay.note: They slowly dry out and lose capacity, faster when hot.
